passages.scripture: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

lines.text: Some believers have strong faith.
Other believers have had weak faith.
We must accept the person whose faith is weak.
Do not judge his thoughts or opinions.

passages.scripture: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

lines.text: One person has strong faith.
This person believes all kinds of food can be eaten.
Another person has weak faith.
This person eats only vegetables.

passages.scripture: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

lines.text: God accepts every believer.
Some people eat all kinds of food.
Some people do not eat everything.
The person who eats everything must not look down on the person who does not eat everything.
The person who does not eat everything must not judge the person who eats everything.

passages.scripture: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

lines.text: We are not the master of another person’s servant.
We do not have the right to judge that servant.
Each servant stands or falls before his own Master.
The Lord is the Master of every servant.
The Lord is the Master of every believer.
Are we the master of another believer?
Are we the one who will judge another believer on judgment day?
The Lord is able to make each of His servants stand.
Each servant will stand because the Lord will provide strength.

passages.scripture: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

lines.text: One person thinks one day is more important than other days.
Another person thinks all days are the same.
Each of us must be fully convinced in our own mind.
Each of us must be fully convinced in our own mind, including about how we honor days or not.

passages.scripture: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

lines.text: A person who observes a special day observes it for the Lord.
A person who eats does so for the Lord.
A person who eats gives thanks to God.
A person who does not eat does this for the Lord.
A person who does not eat also gives thanks to God.

passages.scripture: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

lines.text: No one lives only for himself.
No one dies only for himself.
Each of us belongs to others.
Each of us is connected to others in life and in death.
We do not live or die in isolation.
We live and die connected to each other as members of the body of Christ.

passages.scripture: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

lines.text: As Christians, we belong to the Lord.
If we live, we live for the Lord.
If we die, we die for the Lord.
Whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

passages.scripture: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

lines.text: Christ is the Son of God.
Christ died for us.
Christ returned to life.
Christ did this for a purpose.
Christ became Lord over all people, whether living or dead.
Having died, Christ is Lord over those who have died.
And Christ is Lord over those who are alive.
Christ is Lord over all.

passages.scripture: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

lines.text: Paul asks a question.
Why do you judge your brother?
Or why do you look down on your brother?
God will judge everyone.
We will all stand before the judgment seat of God.

passages.scripture: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

lines.text: God says, “As surely as I live.”
God is making a promise.
Every knee will bow before God.
Every tongue will confess to God.

passages.scripture: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

lines.text: Each person will stand before God.
God will judge every person.
Each of us must answer to God for what we have done in this life.

passages.scripture: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

lines.text: God will be the One to judge each of us.
So we should not judge one another.
We must decide to not put a stumbling block in our brother’s way.
We must not seek for our brother to stumble.
We must not seek for our brother to fall.
We must not seek for our brother to be hurt or harmed.
We must not seek for our brother to sin.
We must decide to do all this.

passages.scripture: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

lines.text: Paul is fully convinced in the Lord Jesus.
Nothing is unclean by itself.
But, if a person thinks something is unclean, then it is unclean for that person.

passages.scripture: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

lines.text: Paul is writing to Christians in Rome.
Paul teaches about love among believers.
Suppose, in our freedom, we eat.
And suppose our brother is distressed because of what we eat.
Then we are not walking in love.
Instead we use our freedom to not eat that in front of them.
And, if we do eat that, then eat in secret where they will not be distressed.
We must not let our eating cause our brother to fall.
We must not let our eating destroy our brother.
Christ died for our brother.

passages.scripture: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

lines.text: We must not let what you think is good to be spoken of as evil.
We must not allow others to call our good actions evil.
If possible, we should something good that is not misunderstood or criticized by fellow believers who are weaker in faith.
However, if someone demands that not do good, then any good we do may be called evil.
We must do what is right in the sight of God, and, if it is possible, then also in the sight of men, but that may not be possible.

passages.scripture: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

lines.text: The kingdom of God does not depend on eating.
The kingdom of God does not depend on drinking.
The kingdom of God is about righteousness.
The kingdom of God is about peace.
The kingdom of God is about joy.
The Holy Spirit gives this righteousness, peace, and joy.

passages.scripture: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

lines.text: Whoever serves Christ in this way pleases God.
God accepts this person.
People also approve of this person.

passages.scripture: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

lines.text: Let us pursue what leads to peace.
Let us also pursue what builds up one another.

passages.scripture: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

lines.text: Do not destroy God’s work because of food.
All food is clean.
But eating becomes wrong if it causes someone to stumble.
It is wrong for someone to let their eating lead another into distress.

passages.scripture: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.

lines.text: If eating meat causes your brother to stumble then it is better to not eat meat.
If what you drink causes your brother to stumble then it is better to not drink that.
When we are in front of other believers, we should not perform actions harm their faith.
And even if our brother cannot see what we're doing to stumble, we should always do what pleases God, for God sees everything.

passages.scripture: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

lines.text: We must keep our belief about our freedom to eat and drink between ourselves and God.
We must not force our weaker brother to be stronger.
God sees our hearts and whether or not we condemn ourselves in our choices.
We are blessed if he do not condemn ourselves by what we approve.
If we do what we believe is right, and our conscience is clear, then we are blessed.

passages.scripture: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

lines.text: A person who has doubts is not sure if God allows eating something.
If someone doubts their eating, he is condemned.
Someone who doubts is not living by faith.
God wants us to live by faith.
Anything not done from faith is sin.
